summary: Drove the running headless substrate (engine ...0001) over MCP. Discovered the aether.tcp vocabulary via describe_kinds (no guide doc exists). bind_listener{addr:"127.0.0.1:0"} replied Ok{listener_name:"34215", listener_id, local_port:34215}. connect{addr:"127.0.0.1:34215"} replied ConnectResult::Ok{session_name:"conn-0", session_id:mbx-urol-s7yl-abyx, peer:"127.0.0.1:34215"} — loopback peer confirmed. session_write{bytes} to "conn-0" was dispatched via send_mail with status "delivered" and no error/session_closed surfaced, so every documented step completed. Caveat surfaced as findings: the returned session_name/session_id is NOT resolvable by send_mail_traced (errors "unknown recipient mailbox") or actor_logs ("not registered"), and send_mail reports "delivered" even for a deliberately-bogus session name — so the write's delivery to the actual session is unverifiable through the harness (likely a silent warn-drop). The connect/connect_result surface itself works as specified. Engine left alive for the judge (headless — capture_frame will Err; TCP produces no visual frame).

artifact.rationale: capture_frame returned no image — the engine settled without a reply event ("frame capture on a windowless/headless substrate emits no frame"). This matches the expected artifact exactly: this is a TCP-transport scenario where nothing renders, so correctness is read from the ConnectResult::Ok reply and absence of a session-close error, not from a frame. There is no renderable artifact to judge visually. Substrate terminated afterward to free the fleet.

papercut.where: session_write to the connect-side session over the MCP harness (send_mail / send_mail_traced / actor_logs)
papercut.what: connect_result returns session_name "conn-0" and a session_id MailboxId, but that address resolves nowhere through the harness: send_mail_traced rejects "conn-0", the raw mbx- id, and every lineage form I tried (aether.tcp/conn-0, aether.tcp:conn-0, aether.tcp/aether.tcp:conn-0) with 'unknown recipient mailbox'; actor_logs says the name is 'not registered'. Plain send_mail reports status "delivered" for "conn-0" — but ALSO reports "delivered" for a deliberately-bogus "conn-does-not-exist-zzz", so its success is a false positive that warn-drops silently. There is no positive-confirmation path that a session_write reached the dialed session; the task's 'confirm no error/close is surfaced' is only satisfiable because the one tool that WOULD surface the failure (send_mail_traced) refuses the address outright.
papercut.suggested: Register each TCP session (and listener) under an addressable lineage name resolvable by ALL mail tools (send_mail, send_mail_traced, actor_logs) — e.g. aether.tcp/aether.embedded:conn-0 — and return that exact addressable string in connect_result.session_name. Separately, make send_mail's warn-drop return a status other than 'delivered' so a mistyped/stale session address is not silently swallowed.

papercut.where: send_mail param encoding for aether.tcp.bind_listener / aether.tcp.connect
papercut.what: describe_kinds renders the field as 'name: Option<String>', but omitting it fails encoding with 'missing required field "$.name"'. An Option-typed field reads as omittable to a consumer; I had to pass an explicit name:null to get past it.
papercut.suggested: Make Option-typed fields omittable in the MCP param encoder (treat a missing Option field as None), or render genuinely-required fields without the Option<> wrapper so the shape doesn't imply an omission that the encoder rejects.

missing-primitive.where: targeting a returned MailboxId (session_id) from the MCP harness
missing-primitive.what: connect_result hands back session_id as a MailboxId, the natural handle for the session, but the harness has no way to send to a raw MailboxId — recipient_name is a name string, and send_mail_traced explicitly rejects the tagged 'mbx-urol-s7yl-abyx' id. describe_component accepts a tagged mbx- id as a fast-path, so the asymmetry is surprising: the id you are handed cannot be used to send to the thing it identifies.
missing-primitive.suggested: Let send_mail / send_mail_traced accept a tagged mbx- id in recipient_name (as describe_component already does) and route directly to that mailbox, so a returned session_id is immediately usable.

doc-gap.where: learning how to use the aether.tcp capability at all (docs/guide/)
doc-gap.what: There is no consumer documentation for aether.tcp anywhere: it is absent from docs/guide/SUMMARY.md (HTTP egress has systems/http.md; TCP has nothing), there is no recipe, and the only grep hit in the guide is a note about tcp/mod.rs file size in capability-anatomy.md. A fresh consumer must reverse-engineer the entire bind_listener/connect/session_write/session_data/session_closed vocabulary from describe_kinds, with no guidance on how session addressing is supposed to work — which is exactly where the flow breaks down.
doc-gap.suggested: Add docs/guide/systems/tcp.md (mirroring http.md) and a SUMMARY entry: document bind_listener/connect/session_write and the session_data/session_closed inbound kinds, the ConnectResult shape, and — critically — the exact recipient string a caller must use to address a returned session over mail.
